cities.name: Ranchi
cities.overview: Jharkhand's capital on the Chota Nagpur plateau, surrounded by waterfalls fed by the Subarnarekha and its tributaries.
cities.history: The summer capital of Bihar in British days and a centre of the Jharkhand movement. It became the capital of the new state of Jharkhand in 2000.

cities.name: Betla
cities.overview: The forest village in Latehar district that serves as the gateway to Betla National Park and the Palamau Tiger Reserve.

cities.name: Deoghar
cities.overview: A temple town in the Santhal Pargana region, built around the Baba Baidyanath Dham.

cities.name: Jamshedpur
cities.overview: India's first planned industrial city, built by the Tatas, with a lake and hills at its door.

cities.name: Giridih
cities.overview: A town near Parasnath, the highest hill in Jharkhand.

cities.name: Latehar
cities.overview: The forest district of Palamu, with Netarhat and Betla.

cities.name: Hazaribagh
cities.overview: A plateau town with a wildlife sanctuary and open-air lakes.

cities.name: Dumka
cities.overview: The main town of the Santhal Pargana, close to the terracotta temples at Maluti.

places.name: Hundru Falls
places.shortDescription: A 98 m waterfall where the Subarnarekha River drops off the Ranchi plateau, about 45 km from the city.
places.description: At Hundru the Subarnarekha River falls about 98 m over the edge of the Ranchi plateau into a rocky pool, one of the highest waterfalls in Jharkhand. Several hundred steps lead down to the base, where the spray is strong in the monsoon. In the dry months the rock shelves around the pool become a popular picnic spot. Swimming is unsafe after rain.
places.history: The Ranchi plateau is known as a land of waterfalls; Hundru, Dassam, Jonha and Hirni falls all lie within a short drive of the city.
places.bestTimeNote: July to October for full flow; November to January for safe picnics at the base.

location.address: Hundru, Angara block, Ranchi district, Jharkhand 835103

places.name: Betla National Park
places.shortDescription: Sal and bamboo forest in the Palamau Tiger Reserve, with elephants, gaur and two ruined hill forts.
places.description: Betla National Park forms the core of the Palamau Tiger Reserve, among the first reserves created under Project Tiger. Jeep safaris pass through sal and bamboo forest and grasslands where elephants, gaur, sambar, langurs and peafowl are common; tigers are rarely seen. Inside the park are the ruins of the old and new Palamau forts, built by the Chero kings. Watchtowers overlook waterholes near the entrance.
places.history: Palamau was one of the nine original tiger reserves declared under Project Tiger in 1973. The Chero dynasty ruled Palamau from these forts until the 18th century.
places.bestTimeNote: November to April. The park is generally closed in the monsoon.

entryFee.note: Entry, vehicle and guide fees are charged at the gate.

places.name: Baidyanath Temple
places.shortDescription: Baba Baidyanath Dham, one of the twelve Jyotirlinga shrines of Shiva and a Shakti Peetha.
places.description: The Baidyanath temple complex in Deoghar holds the main Shiva shrine and 21 smaller temples within its walls. During the month of Shravan (July–August) the Shravani Mela draws millions of kanwariyas who walk about 105 km from Sultanganj carrying Ganga water to offer to the lingam. Queues are long through the festival season. The nearby Trikut hills and Naulakha Mandir make good side trips.
places.history: Baidyanath is counted among the twelve Jyotirlingas and the 51 Shakti Peethas. The main temple is traditionally associated with the legend of Ravana and Shiva's healing form as Vaidyanath, the lord of physicians.
places.bestTimeNote: October to March is comfortable; July–August is the Shravani Mela, the most crowded and devotional time.

entryFee.note: Free entry; a paid quick-darshan option is available.

timings.hours: About 4:00 AM – 9:00 PM, closed briefly in the afternoon

places.name: Dassam Falls
places.shortDescription: A waterfall near Ranchi, dropping about 44 m from the Kanchi River in a rocky forest setting.
places.description: A loud, wide drop into a stony pool. Swimming has proved dangerous here, so stick to the viewpoints.

places.name: Jonha Falls
places.shortDescription: A waterfall in Ranchi district, reached by over 700 steps down to the base.
places.description: Also called Gautamdhara, with a temple to the Buddha at the top. It's reached by rail, or by road through forest.

places.name: Jagannath Temple, Ranchi
places.shortDescription: A 1691 hilltop temple at Ranchi, in the style of the Jagannath Temple at Puri, with a big Rath Yatra.
places.description: Rebuilt after a partial collapse, it's a smaller version of the Puri temple. Its Rath Yatra fair is the biggest in the state.

places.name: Rock Garden, Ranchi
places.shortDescription: A garden of stone sculptures on Gonda Hill in Ranchi, next to Kanke Dam.
places.description: Rocks and statues on a hilltop with views over the dam. It's a popular family outing on weekends.

places.name: Rajrappa
places.shortDescription: A waterfall and Chhinnamasta temple at the meeting of the Damodar and Bhera rivers.
places.description: A goddess shrine known as a major Shakti site in the region, with a small waterfall on the Bhera close by.

places.name: Dimna Lake
places.shortDescription: An artificial lake 15 km from Jamshedpur, under the Dalma Hills, popular for water sports.
places.description: A Tata-built reservoir with a calm shore and the Dalma Range behind it. Sunset is the best time to visit.

places.name: Dalma Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A hill sanctuary near Jamshedpur, known for its elephants.
places.description: A short climb or drive into forest with watchtowers. There's a Shiva temple at the top of the hill.

places.name: Parasnath Hill
places.shortDescription: The highest peak in Jharkhand, also a key Jain pilgrimage site with many temples.
places.description: Pilgrims walk barefoot up a 27 km circuit, to temples marking where many Jain Tirthankaras attained liberation.

places.name: Netarhat
places.shortDescription: A quiet plateau hill town in Latehar, known as the Queen of Chotanagpur, with pine trees and sunsets.
places.description: A high plateau of pine and tribal villages. Magnolia Point is famous for sunset, and Lodh Falls is within reach.

places.name: Lodh Falls
places.shortDescription: The tallest waterfall in Jharkhand, on the Burha River within Palamau Tiger Reserve.
places.description: A long drop in remote forest, with a walk in from the road. It's at its best just after the monsoon.

places.name: Hazaribagh Wildlife Sanctuary
places.shortDescription: A plateau forest about 55 miles north of Ranchi, established in 1955.
places.description: Sal forest, watchtowers and a broad forest drive. It's a quiet, little-visited area.

places.name: Maluti Temples
places.shortDescription: A village near Dumka with over 70 surviving terracotta temples of the Baj Basanta dynasty.
places.description: A remarkable group of small brick temples with terracotta panels showing epics and village scenes. It's still little known.
